_comment: Ceiling on unresolvable citations in docs/*.md, enforced by tools/validate.py.
BASELINE: 8 when this check was added -- the measured count, so CI went
green on the committed debt and red on any NEW rotted citation.
(reproduce the count with: python tools/validate.py)
A docs citation that resolves to nothing degrades to inline code instead of a
link (rewrite_docs in tools/build_site_data.py), so before this file existed
the failure was invisible: the doc rendered, the site built, and nothing
failed. validate.py never read docs/ at all.
It is already ratcheting down as the citations get fixed; this file is kept
at the CURRENT count so a single new one fails CI. When a change REDUCES the
count, lower this in that same change -- validate.py prints the exact figure
to copy. Never RAISE it to make CI pass.
See DOCS_BUDGET_NOTE in tools/validate.py.
The 8 baseline citations, measured 2026-10-08 against 3,979 records across
all 27 docs/*.md files, and confirmed by a second method -- feeding each
citation to rewrite_docs() and counting the ones that come back as inline
code -- which agrees exactly:
06-glossary.md:300                 [SCHEMA.md](../SCHEMA.md)
06-glossary.md:301                 [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md)
07-benchmarking-methodology.md:11  [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md)
07-benchmarking-methodology.md:289 [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md)
07-benchmarking-methodology.md:291 [SCHEMA.md](../SCHEMA.md)
16-migration-upgrade.md:201        [15-cost-per-token.md](15-cost-per-token.md)
17-deployment-shape.md:205         [15-cost-per-token.md](15-cost-per-token.md)
18-reliability.md:284              [15-cost-per-token.md](15-cost-per-token.md)
Two classes, because the fix differs:
* 5 links point at SCHEMA.md / AGENTS.md, which are REAL files at the repo
root. The docs citation grammar resolves a .md target against docs/ stems
only, so they degrade to plain text on the live site. They are links the
renderer cannot express, not rot.
* 3 are genuine rot: 15-cost-per-token.md was renumbered to
08-cost-per-token.md and no 15- file exists, so the pointer is dead.
This is the failure mode the check was written to find, and the first
thing to fix -- fixing it takes the count to 5 and this budget in the
same change.
Fixing them is a docs/ content edit, which is out of this change's scope, so
they are shipped as budgeted debt rather than repaired here.
